items.title: Codex-exec runner for the onboarding runtime follow-on

prompt: Work item: uaa-0022 — Codex-exec runner for the onboarding runtime follow-on.
Goal: replace the current manual translation of the operator-guide runtime lane with a bounded Codex execution recipe that starts after `onboard-agent` and `scaffold-wrapper-crate`.
Key decisions already made:
- Default baseline is `opencode`-level support.
- `gemini_cli` is a minimal exception path only and requires explicit justification.
- `codex` and `claude_code` remain feature-rich references for optional richer surfaces.
Steps:
1) Define the runtime-lane input contract: which packet files, registry fields, and scaffold outputs the runner reads.
2) Define the output contract: runtime code, wrapper coverage source-of-truth, committed manifest evidence, and an achieved-tier summary.
3) Define the instruction recipe so Codex defaults to the `opencode` template and only pulls in `gemini_cli` / `codex` / `claude_code` patterns when justified.
4) Define the review requirement for `minimal` outcomes: explicit justification plus follow-up work to reach `default`.
Output: a repo-owned runner plan ready for implementation, without reopening the operator guide or folding in publication-refresh follow-on work.
deliverables: Pinned runtime-lane runner input/output contract
Pinned tiering policy for default/minimal/feature-rich runtime implementations
Implementation-ready execution recipe for Codex to complete the runtime follow-on

notes: This is the next create-mode automation seam after the recommendation lane and M6 control-plane boundary.
The runner should start from the operator-guide runtime follow-on, not from an open-ended request to 'copy existing backends'.

Default means `opencode`-level support. Minimal means `gemini_cli`-level support and requires explicit justification. Feature-rich means selectively borrowing richer patterns from `codex` and `claude_code`.
Keep publication refresh automation after runtime evidence exists as a separate follow-up milestone.

Implemented on 2026-04-29: `xtask runtime-follow-on` landed, the create-mode operator guide now uses the bounded runtime packet, and the runner emits a validated handoff into the publication and green gates.

items.title: Obs facet schema (events + completion)

prompt: Work item: uaa-0014 — Obs facet schema (events + completion).
Goal: define a stable, bounded obs metadata schema that can carry run_id / trace_context / tags across AgentWrapperEvent.data and AgentWrapperCompletion.data.

Key constraint: ToolCall/ToolResult events already use `data.schema = agent_api.tools.structured.v1`; obs metadata must coexist without breaking the tools facet contract (likely via an optional nested `obs` object in `data`, not a competing top-level schema for tool events).
Steps:
1) Specify the obs object shape + strict bounds (identifiers + small maps only; no raw backend lines).
2) Specify where the obs data MAY appear (which event kinds, completion.data) and merge/precedence rules when both caller and backend supply context.
3) Specify how this schema relates to upcoming surfaces: agent_api.obs.run_id.v1, agent_api.obs.trace_context.v1, agent_api.obs.tags.v1.
Output: spec text updates ready for implementation (keep it conservative and backward-compatible with existing tools facet rules).
deliverables: A concrete obs facet schema (v1) + placement rules + bounds, suitable to unblock run_id/trace_context/tags work

notes: Define a single bounded obs facet schema carried in AgentWrapperEvent.data and/or AgentWrapperCompletion.data (AgentWrapperEvent has no top-level run/session/trace fields).
This facet should be the foundation for: agent_api.obs.run_id.v1, agent_api.obs.trace_context.v1, agent_api.obs.tags.v1.
Decide emission model: always emit vs gated by explicit capabilities and/or an extension key; define precedence + merge rules when both backend and caller supply context.
Draft spec text (backlog-only): docs/backlog/uaa-0014-obs-facet-schema-v1.md
On hold. This is not a priority right now.

prompt: Work item: uaa-0017 — Add typed session/thread id accessors (codex + claude_code).
Goal: add small helper accessors on the typed backend event models so downstream crates can extract a stable session/thread identifier without duplicating match logic.
Steps:

items.title: P1: Restrict selection-failure translation to actual not-found errors

prompt: Work item: uaa-0018 — P1: Restrict selection-failure translation to actual not-found errors.

Goal: ensure resume/fork selection failures map to pinned safe messages only when the backend truly indicates a not-found condition; do not mislabel unrelated backend failures as "no session found" / "session not found".
Primary impact: Claude Code backend (agent_api) currently infers selection failure from non-success exit + no assistant output and suppresses ResultError events, masking real failure causes.
Steps:
1) Adjust Claude backend selection-failure detection to rely on explicit not-found signals (e.g., structured ResultError payload or stable not-found indicator), not absence-of-output.
2) Ensure non-not-found failures surface as AgentWrapperError::Backend with a safe/redacted message and emit a single terminal Error event when events are available.
3) Add regression tests: generic resume/fork failure with no assistant output must NOT translate to the pinned selection-failure messages.
Output: correct error classification + pinned selection failures + tests; no backend secrets leak.
deliverables: Selection-failure translation restricted to actual not-found signals (Claude Code)
Regression tests preventing false-positive "session not found" translations

notes: Do not infer selection failure solely from non-zero exit + no assistant output (false positives).
If ResultError events are suppressed for safety, still use their typed/raw payload for classification, and surface a generic safe error for non-not-found failures.

items.title: Beware: Claude stream-json result subtype drift when promoting versions

prompt: Work item: uaa-0019 — Beware: Claude stream-json result subtype drift when promoting versions.

Context: A newer local Claude CLI (e.g., 2.1.63) emitted `type:"result"` with a non-v1 `subtype` (e.g., "error_during_execution") for resume-by-id not-found. This does not parse as `ClaudeStreamJsonEvent::ResultError` under the current v1 parser contract (success/error only), which can break downstream selection-failure translation that relies on ResultError.raw classification.

Goal: when raising Claude Code coverage and/or promoting `cli_manifests/claude_code/latest_validated.txt`, validate stream-json result taxonomy against the candidate binary and update the parser contract + fixtures as needed before promotion.
Steps:
1) Run stream-json spot checks against the candidate `claude` binary (not whatever happens to be on PATH) for: resume id not-found, resume last empty, generic failure.

2) If result subtypes differ from v1 (success/error), update `crates/claude_code` stream-json parser + the normative parser specs/fixtures to accept the new subtype(s) (while keeping safety/redaction posture).
3) Re-validate `agent_api` selection-failure translation against the candidate binary once the parser emits typed ResultError events again.
Output: promotion-safe parser contract updates (specs + fixtures + code) that keep higher Claude versions from silently regressing session error translation.
deliverables: Updated Claude stream-json parser contract/fixtures for new result subtype(s)
Evidence the candidate Claude version preserves typed ResultError emission for agent_api

notes: Avoid validating against an arbitrary local `claude` on PATH; use the binary under promotion and compare to cli_manifests pointers.
If new result subtypes appear, treat it as a promotion gate: update parser contract + fixtures before bumping latest_validated/min_supported.

items.title: P2: Enforce 1024-byte handle id bound for Codex fork thread IDs

prompt: Work item: uaa-0020 — P2: Enforce 1024-byte handle id bound for Codex fork thread IDs.
Goal: ensure the Codex fork path treats oversize thread ids (>1024 bytes) as unknown (omit session handle facet; SHOULD warn) per the session handle facet contract.

Context: Codex exec/resume path enforces the bound before storing thread_id, but the fork path stores any non-empty id, allowing oversize ids to leak into handle facets via app-server notifications and completion data.
Steps:
1) Update `crates/agent_api/src/backends/codex/fork.rs` to enforce the 1024-byte bound before storing the forked thread id (and treat oversize as unknown).
2) Emit a safe `Status` warning once per run when an oversize id is observed (align with the exec/resume warning marker in `crates/agent_api/src/backends/codex.rs`).

3) Add regression tests by extending the fake codex app-server test binary to return an oversize forked thread id, and assert the handle facet is omitted in both events and completion (and warning emitted if implemented).
Output: consistent bound enforcement across Codex exec + fork paths; no contract violations.
deliverables: Bound enforcement for forked thread ids (<=1024 bytes)
Regression tests for oversize forked thread ids

notes: Contract: ids over 1024 bytes must be treated as unknown (omit facet; MUST NOT truncate); SHOULD warn.
Keep behavior consistent across Codex exec/resume and Codex fork flows.

items.title: Claude: persistent project-scoped state isolation parity (.claude / .mcp.json)

prompt: Work item: uaa-0021 — Claude: persistent project-scoped state isolation parity (.claude / .mcp.json).

Goal: design and implement Codex-like persistent, app-managed project state isolation for Claude runs so project-scoped Claude artifacts are redirected away from the real repo while preserving access to the real workspace.

Context: `claude_home` only isolates user-scoped state (`~/.claude*`). Claude also discovers project-scoped state from the working tree, including `.claude/settings*.json`, `.claude/agents`, `.claude/commands`, hooks/memory files, `CLAUDE.md`, and `.mcp.json`. A stop-gap `agent_api` `claude_home` wiring can ship independently, but it does not solve project-local state isolation.
Steps:

1) Inventory which Claude surfaces are discovered from cwd/project root vs user home, and pin the minimum parity target for v1 (at least `.claude/**`, `.mcp.json`, and `CLAUDE.md` discovery semantics).
2) Design a persistent app-managed project-root layout/overlay in `crates/claude_code` that can host isolated Claude project files while still exposing the real workspace contents to the CLI.

3) Decide how the wrapper selects and materializes that project overlay across repeated runs (persistent per app/project key, not one tempdir per run), including cleanup/update behavior and cross-platform filesystem strategy.

4) Evaluate where existing Claude flags (`--settings`, `--setting-sources`, `--mcp-config`) can be reused for subsets of the problem versus where project-root overlay behavior is still required for parity.

5) Expose the new project-state isolation controls through `crates/claude_code` first, then add host-facing `agent_api` config + canonical spec text only once the behavior is implemented and testable.
6) Add end-to-end tests proving Claude reads/writes isolated `.claude` / `.mcp.json` content under the app-managed root rather than the real repo, without regressing normal workspace file access.
Output: a concrete crate/API design plus implementation plan for full Claude project-state isolation; keep the smaller `claude_home` stop-gap tracked separately and unblocked.
deliverables: A persistent project-overlay design for Claude project-scoped state
An implementation plan for exposing the feature in claude_code and then agent_api
A test strategy covering isolated `.claude` and `.mcp.json` behavior

notes: Do not treat `claude_home` as sufficient parity: it isolates user-home state, not project-local `.claude` / `.mcp.json` discovery.
Prefer a persistent app-managed directory keyed per app/project over ephemeral tempdirs so repeated runs share the same isolated Claude project state.
Likely requires new `claude_code` crate primitives first; `agent_api` should only surface the config after the lower-level behavior exists.
The stop-gap `ClaudeCodeBackendConfig.claude_home` wiring can land independently and should not be blocked on this larger feature.
Needs new crate support for a persistent project overlay/root that redirects project-scoped Claude discovery (`.claude/**`, `.mcp.json`, `CLAUDE.md`) while preserving access to the real workspace.
Serves as the parity reference for app-managed persistent state isolation, but Codex's native `CODEX_HOME` model is user-home scoped and does not directly solve Claude's project-root discovery model.

items.title: Typed errors for support-audit evidence faults (remove exit-code string matching)

prompt: Work item: uaa-0023 — Typed errors for support-audit evidence faults.

Context: `maintenance-audit-status` is a CI gate whose exit code is its product (0 clean, 3 uplifts required, 2 validation/bad evidence, 1 internal). `crates/xtask/src/agent_maintenance/support_audit.rs` returns untyped `String` errors, which reach the request layer as `MaintenanceRequestError::Internal`. To classify bad evidence as 2 rather than 1, `audit_status.rs` currently pattern-matches on error message text in `is_bad_support_audit_evidence_message` (matching `parse `, ` is missing `deltas` object`, ` is missing `deltas.`, `support-audit report row`).

Why this is debt: classification by message string is silently fragile — editing a message in `support_audit.rs` changes a gate exit code with no compile error and no failing test. An equivalent string-matching approach was already removed once as a defect during T1 (commit d41bb279 replaced it with a real `AuditDriftPolicy`).

Severity note: the failure direction is safe. A message drift makes the match fail, leaving the error `Internal` -> exit 1, which fails CI loudly. It cannot produce a false clean (0) or swallow an uplift (3). This is fragility, not a correctness hole — schedule it, do not treat it as urgent.

Goal: give `support_audit.rs` a typed error that distinguishes bad evidence data from I/O/internal faults, thread it through the request layer, and delete `is_bad_support_audit_evidence_message` entirely.
Steps:
1) Introduce a typed error enum in `support_audit.rs` separating evidence-data faults (malformed JSON, missing `deltas` object/arrays, malformed report rows) from I/O and internal faults.
2) Preserve the distinction across `request.rs` / `MaintenanceRequestError` rather than collapsing to `Internal`.
3) Delete `is_bad_support_audit_evidence_message` from `audit_status.rs` and the `From` impl branch that calls it.
4) Confirm `refresh`, `prepare`, `closeout`, and `execute` are bit-for-bit unaffected — they run under `AuditDriftPolicy::Reject` and must not change behavior.
5) Keep the existing exit-code tests green, and add one that would fail if a message were edited (i.e. assert on the typed variant, not the text).
Output: no exit-code classification anywhere in the maintenance lane depends on error message text.
deliverables: Typed evidence-vs-internal error in support_audit.rs
is_bad_support_audit_evidence_message deleted
Exit-code tests that assert on typed variants rather than message text

notes: Introduced by T1 remediation round 5 (commit b55cef4f) as a deliberate, documented compromise: the round-5 packet scoped support_audit.rs out of the write set to avoid regression risk in shared code.
Failure direction is safe (worst case exit 1, never a false clean), which is why it was deferred rather than blocking T1.

items.title: Define union-vs-per-target coverage coherence contract

prompt: Work item: uaa-0024 — Define a union-vs-per-target coverage coherence contract.

Context: `maintenance-audit-status` derives the live support-surface audit from a single selected coverage report (`select_report_path` prefers `coverage.any.json`, then `coverage.all.json`, then the first `coverage.*.json` by sort order). Since T1 round 5 the gate also requires that every `coverage.*.json` in the version directory declares the correct `inputs.upstream.semantic_version`, and that `snapshots/<version>/union.json` has `complete=true`.

Gap: nothing validates that the union report's contents are actually consistent with the per-target reports it claims to summarize. A per-target report can be stale or partial in content while still carrying the right version string and sitting alongside a complete union.
Why it was deferred: closing this requires first defining what coherence means between the union and its per-target inputs — a contract that does not exist today. It is a design task, not a bug fix.

Goal: decide and document whether the union is authoritative-by-construction (per-target reports being provenance only), or whether the gate should cross-validate, and implement whichever the contract says.
Steps:
1) Determine how `crates/xtask/src/manifest_report.rs` builds `coverage.any.json` / `coverage.all.json` from per-target inputs, and whether the union is reconstructible from them.
2) Decide the contract: authoritative union (document it and close this item), or cross-validated union (specify exactly which fields must agree).
3) If cross-validating, implement it in the acquisition/report-generation lane rather than in the audit gate, so the invariant holds at write time rather than being re-checked at read time.
4) Record the decision where the maintenance lifecycle docs will surface it.
Output: a written coherence contract, and either an implementation or an explicit documented decision that the union is authoritative.
deliverables: Written union-vs-per-target coherence contract
Implementation at report-generation time, or a documented authoritative-union decision

notes: Raised by the Codex review lane during T1 remediation round 4 review; adjudicated as a real limitation but deferred because the contract it depends on does not exist yet.
Distinct from the completeness defect fixed in b55cef4f: that one was about whether the acquisition finished, this one is about whether its outputs agree.

items.title: maintenance-audit-status projection can survive a failed run as a stale result

prompt: Work item: uaa-0025 — `maintenance-audit-status` projection can survive a failed run as a stale result.

Context: `--emit-json` writes an `AuditStatusProjection` carrying `schema_version` and `request_sha256`. `request_sha256` arrived in T1 remediation round 4 (commit 4620b531) so a consumer could detect a stale projection file. The projection carries no timestamp, to keep output byte-identical across runs.

Original defect (T1 r4 adversarial lane): the hash cannot detect same-request staleness. Re-running the same request produces the same hash, so a projection left by an earlier clean run is indistinguishable from a fresh one.

T2a (72191bb3) added three-case cleanup: a failure classified preflight preserves an existing projection; a failure classified attempted removes it; a failed fresh write removes it and warns. This was marked closed, then disproved by the T2 adversarial lane (finding M3) with a probe test.

Mechanism (probe-proven): `derive_audit_status` classifies the whole request load as `DeriveAuditStatusFailure::preflight`. But `request::load_request_envelope_validated_with_policy` calls `validate_support_surface_audit`, which runs `derive_support_surface_audit`, a full live derivation. Every check `request.rs` runs after it (`validate_execution_contract`, `validate_automated_watch_request`, `validate_rfc3339_utc`, `validate_commit_value`) therefore fails as preflight, and projection cleanup is skipped.
Probe: an invalid `request_commit` plus uplift-requiring evidence exits 2, and a pre-seeded projection claiming `uplifts_required: false` survives.
Second route: `is_bad_support_audit_evidence_message` downgrades a corrupt live coverage report to `Validation` along the same preflight path, which also preserves the stale file.

Naming (T2 Codex lane F4): evidence failures are classified attempted before `derive_support_surface_audit` runs. Adjudicated as correct behaviour, because the run read live evidence and found it bad, but the flag name `live_derivation_attempted` misdescribes it. Rename as part of this item.

Silent cleanup failure (T2 Codex lane F3): on the post-derivation failure path the removal error is discarded (`let _ = remove_projection(path)` in `run_in_workspace`, `audit_status.rs`), while the fresh-write path warns on stderr. Make the two paths consistent.

Why it is latent today (T2 adversarial lane L9): CI writes the projection to `_ci_tmp/audit/status.json` and deletes `_ci_tmp` unread before commit. T3 is the first consumer. Fix this with or before T3.
Steps:

1) Decide the rule: fix the preflight/attempted classification so any failure after the request load's internal derivation removes the projection, or declare the exit code the only authority and state that the JSON is strictly advisory (and make T3 read it only after exit 0 or 3 from the same invocation).
2) Rename `live_derivation_attempted` to describe what it actually records.
3) Warn on stderr when post-derivation cleanup fails, matching the fresh-write path.
4) Add regression tests: the invalid-`request_commit` probe, the corrupt-coverage-report route, and the clean-then-stale two-run scenario.
5) Confirm `refresh`, `prepare`, `closeout`, and `execute` stay bit-for-bit unaffected under `AuditDriftPolicy::Reject`.
Output: no failed run can leave a projection that a consumer would read as a current result, or an explicit, enforced exit-code-is-authoritative rule.
deliverables: Correct preflight/attempted classification, or a documented and enforced exit-code-is-authoritative rule
Renamed classification flag
Stderr warning when post-derivation projection cleanup fails
Regression tests for the request-validation probe, the corrupt-report route, and the two-run stale-file scenario

notes: Found by the Opus adversarial review lane during T1 remediation round 4 review.
Marked closed during T2a (72191bb3) and reopened within the hour after the T2 adversarial lane disproved the fix (finding M3, probe test).
Folds in T2 Codex lane F4 (flag naming), T2 Codex lane F3 (silent cleanup failure), and T2 adversarial lane L9 (why it is latent).
Fix with or before T3, which is the first consumer of the projection.

items.title: maintenance-audit-status loses exit 3 when --emit-json cannot be written

prompt: Work item: uaa-0026 — `maintenance-audit-status` loses exit 3 when `--emit-json` cannot be written.
Context: exit 3 (uplifts required) is a result, not an error — CI branches on it to open a contributor relay packet. The outcome is computed before the projection is written.

Defect: if `write_projection_atomically` fails (unwritable path, full disk, permissions), the `?` propagates the write error and the already-computed `UpliftsRequired` outcome is discarded, so the command exits 1 instead of 3. A genuine uplift-required state is reported as an internal fault.

Status: pre-existing, not introduced by any T1 remediation round. Low impact in practice because a workflow that routes 'anything other than 0 or 3' to failure still stops, and the underlying write failure is itself worth failing on.
Goal: decide whether the outcome or the write failure takes precedence, and make it explicit rather than incidental.
Steps:
1) Decide precedence: report exit 3 and log the write failure to stderr, or keep failing on the write. Either is defensible — the current behavior is an accident of `?` placement, not a decision.
2) Implement it explicitly in `run_in_workspace` in `crates/xtask/src/agent_maintenance/audit_status.rs`.
3) Add a test that pins the chosen precedence (an unwritable `--emit-json` target on an uplift-producing input).
4) Make sure it agrees with however T2 routes exit codes in `.github/workflows/parity-acquire.yml`.
Output: explicit, tested precedence between a computed outcome and a projection write failure.
deliverables: Explicit precedence between computed outcome and projection write failure
Test pinning the chosen behavior

notes: Observed by the Opus adversarial review lane during T1 remediation round 4 review; confirmed pre-existing rather than introduced by T1.

Implemented in 72191bb3 (T2a): the computed outcome takes precedence. When the fresh --emit-json write fails, the command removes any existing projection, prints a stderr warning, and still returns exit 0 or 3. Pinned by `uplift_outcome_survives_unwritable_emit_json_target_and_warns`, `clean_outcome_survives_unwritable_emit_json_target`, and `failing_fresh_emit_json_write_removes_stale_projection`.

items.title: Snapshot capture retry can mix two attempts in the raw_help artifact

prompt: Work item: uaa-0027 — Snapshot capture retry can mix two attempts in the raw_help artifact.

Context: T2b (e87a9a1d) made the per-target "Generate the per-target snapshot" step in `.github/workflows/parity-acquire.yml` retry the capture once in place (a two-attempt loop with `set +e` / `$?` / `set -e` capture).

Defect (T2 adversarial lane L7): the loop never clears attempt 1's `raw_help/<version>/<target>/` before attempt 2. The uploaded raw-help artifact can therefore contain files from both captures. Nothing compares the two attempts.
Severity: low. raw_help is evidence hygiene only; it is never committed (AGENTS.md hygiene rule), and the snapshot itself comes from the successful attempt.
Steps:
1) Clear the target's raw_help directory at the start of each attempt, keeping the loop portable to bash 3.2 and Git Bash.
2) Extend `c4_spec_reusable_acquisition_retries_snapshot_capture_once_in_place` so it binds the clear-before-retry property.
Output: a raw-help artifact that always comes from exactly one capture attempt.
deliverables: Per-attempt raw_help clear in the retry loop
Contract test binding the property

notes: Raised by the T2 adversarial review lane (L7); accepted and deferred during T2 adjudication.

items.title: maintenance-audit-status deletes whatever path --emit-json names

prompt: Work item: uaa-0028 — `maintenance-audit-status` deletes whatever path `--emit-json` names.

Context: projection cleanup (`remove_projection` in `crates/xtask/src/agent_maintenance/audit_status.rs`) removes the file at the `--emit-json` path on a post-derivation failure or a failed fresh write.

Suspected defect (T2 adversarial lane L8, not probe-proven): there is no ownership guard. The command removes any existing file at that path, whether or not an earlier `maintenance-audit-status` run wrote it.
Why it is low today: CI points `--emit-json` at `_ci_tmp/audit/status.json`, a scratch path. It matters once T3 points `--emit-json` somewhere durable.
Steps:
1) Confirm the behaviour with a test against a pre-existing unrelated file.
2) Decide a guard, for example remove only a file that parses as an `AuditStatusProjection` with a known `schema_version`, and otherwise fail without deleting.
3) Coordinate with uaa-0025, which changes when cleanup runs.
Output: cleanup that cannot delete a file the command did not write.
deliverables: Ownership guard on projection removal
Test proving an unrelated file at the --emit-json path survives

notes: Raised by the T2 adversarial review lane (L8), labelled suspected; accepted and deferred during T2 adjudication.
Resolve before or with T3 if T3 makes the projection path durable.

items.title: parity-acquire does not export the audit gate outputs to callers

prompt: Work item: uaa-0029 — `parity-acquire` does not export the audit gate outputs to callers.

Context: the `union` job in `.github/workflows/parity-acquire.yml` declares job outputs `closeout_ready` and `uplifts_required` from the `maintenance_audit` step. A reusable workflow's caller sees only outputs mapped under `on.workflow_call.outputs` (`outputs.<name>.value: ${{ jobs.union.outputs.<name> }}`).

Defect (found reading code while writing the 2026-09-13 handoff, H1; not yet through a review lane): `on.workflow_call` declares `inputs` and `secrets` but no `outputs`. The only caller, the `acquire` job in `.github/workflows/agent-maintenance-open-pr.yml`, cannot see either value. T2b's packet required them to be consumable by callers; neither review lane caught the gap.
Severity: medium, latent. Nothing consumes the outputs yet. T3 renders the verdict and relay invocation in the caller, so this blocks T3.
Steps:
1) Add `on.workflow_call.outputs` for `closeout_ready`, `uplifts_required`, and probably `audit_exit_code`.
2) Add a contract test in `crates/xtask/tests/c4_spec_ci_wiring.rs` that binds every gate output the `union` job declares to a `workflow_call` output.
3) Grant `pull-requests: write` on whichever caller job renders into the packet PR (T3).
Output: the caller can read the gate verdict without parsing logs.
deliverables: on.workflow_call.outputs for the gate verdict
Contract test binding job outputs to workflow_call outputs

notes: Found while writing the 2026-09-13 handoff (H1). Confirmed by reading; unreviewed.
T3 prerequisite.

items.title: One failed snapshot leg skips the parity-acquire union job and discards the other legs

prompt: Work item: uaa-0030 — One failed snapshot leg skips the `parity-acquire` union job and discards the other legs.

Context: since 68f7fb27 the `union` job in `.github/workflows/parity-acquire.yml` has `needs: [plan, snapshot]`, no status-function `if:`, and the snapshot legs have no `continue-on-error`. `fail-fast: false` keeps the other legs running, but under GitHub's default `needs` semantics any failed leg skips `union`.

Finding (found reading code while writing the 2026-09-13 handoff, H2; confirmed by reading, not observed on a runner): a leg whose capture fails both retry attempts skips the union, the maintenance audit gate, the commit, and the artifact bundle upload. Only the successful legs' per-target artifacts survive, at `retention-days: 1`.

Doc error, corrected 2026-09-13: spec §8.2 and plan §18.1 / §18.4 said acquisition continues on a partial matrix by design. The job graph does not. The materialize step's "union will still be written with complete=false" comment fits only a leg that succeeds but whose snapshot artifact never arrives.

Consequence: exit 4 (incomplete acquisition) is close to unreachable in CI, because the matrix `include` and `union.expected_targets` come from the same list (`crates/xtask/src/manifest_acquisition/plan.rs`). Exit 4 still matters for local runs against committed history: five of seven committed codex acquisitions are `complete: false`.

Policy fit: the maintainer's matrix-flake policy (2026-07-25: retry missing legs once, then fail), implemented as a step-level retry inside each leg, matches this behaviour. But one failed leg discards every other leg's work, the same destroy-work class T2c fixed for the gate step.

Decided 2026-09-13 by the maintainer: preserve completed legs. `union` runs whenever the run was not cancelled and `plan` succeeded (for example `if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.plan.result == 'success' }}`). The union is then written with `complete: false`, the gate routes exit 4, commit and artifact bundle upload still run, and the terminal failure step still fails the job. This is the same record-then-fail pattern T2c applied to the gate step.
Steps:
1) Change the `union` job condition in `.github/workflows/parity-acquire.yml` as decided.
2) Confirm that a failed leg reaches the gate as exit 4 with `missing_targets` naming it, that commit (when `commit: true`) and upload run, and that the job still ends failed.
3) Confirm a failed or skipped `plan` job still skips `union`, and a cancelled run does not commit.
4) Add a contract test in `crates/xtask/tests/c4_spec_ci_wiring.rs` binding the condition and the ordering.
Output: one failed leg no longer discards the other legs' work, and the run still fails.
deliverables: union job condition that preserves completed legs
Contract test binding the condition

notes: Found while writing the 2026-09-13 handoff (H2). Confirmed by reading; not observed on a runner; unreviewed.
The T2 adversarial lane (L6) noted in passing that union is skipped; nobody corrected the docs then.
Doc premise corrected in the spec §8.2 and plan §18.1 / §18.4 on 2026-09-13.
Maintainer decision 2026-09-13: preserve completed legs. Implement in the fix packet that follows the T2c review round.

T2c review round (2026-09-13, both lanes) found the decided rule cannot cover a failed REQUIRED target: the materialize step exits 1 and `manifest-union` independently refuses to build without `union.required_target` (`manifest_union.rs` MissingRequiredSnapshot). Maintainer refinement 2026-09-13: a required-target failure still hard-fails with no union; only non-required leg failures preserve work (union complete=false, exit 4, commit and upload, then fail).

Implemented in a3c8ce53 (T2d): `union` has `if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.plan.result == 'success' }}`; a failed non-required leg yields complete=false, exit 4, commit and upload, then the terminal step fails the job; a failed required target still hard-fails in the materialize step. Bound by `union_job_runs_after_snapshot_failure_but_not_plan_failure_or_cancellation`. Not yet observed on a runner.

items.title: A blocking audit verdict is not visible on the packet PR

prompt: Work item: uaa-0031 — A blocking audit verdict is not visible on the packet PR.

Context: T2c (24a95b52) records the gate verdict and fails the `union` job in a terminal step so that, per its rationale, the packet PR stays red. The gate runs only inside `.github/workflows/parity-acquire.yml`, called by `.github/workflows/agent-maintenance-open-pr.yml`, which the release watcher starts with `createWorkflowDispatch` on `ref: DISPATCH_REF` (`.github/workflows/agent-maintenance-release-watch.yml`).

Finding (H3; suspected in the 2026-09-13 handoff, confirmed by runner observation on 2026-09-14): the `acquire` run is dispatched on `staging`, not triggered by the packet branch, so its check runs attach to the `staging` head commit. The packet PR's checks come only from `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`pull_request` / `push`), which never runs `maintenance-audit-status`. With `commit: true`, an exit-2, exit-4, or exit-5 verdict still pushes artifacts, and the PR shows green checks while the failure is visible only in the watcher-side run. Exit 3 has the same visibility gap, which T3 exists to close.
Steps:

1) Decide where the verdict and the relay invocation become visible: PR body, PR comment, or a commit status / check run created through the API on the packet head SHA. The acquire job's own check run cannot be the surface, because it attaches to `staging`.
2) Implement in the caller after `acquire` (needs uaa-0029 outputs, plus `pull-requests: write` or `statuses: write` / `checks: write` for the chosen surface), with a contract test.
Output: a maintainer looking at the packet PR sees a blocking verdict and an uplift verdict without opening the watcher-side run.
deliverables: Decided visibility surface for the verdict, implemented with T3

notes: Found while writing the 2026-09-13 handoff (H3). Suspected at the time; unreviewed.
T3 design input.

T2c review round (Opus lane F2, 2026-09-13): on exit 3 the `required_uplifts` detail is written only to `_ci_tmp/audit/status.json`, which the cleanup step deletes before commit and upload; with `--emit-json` stdout is empty, so the log does not carry it either. Deferred to T3, which renders the verdict and relay invocation and is the projection's first consumer (resolve uaa-0025 first).

Runner observation (2026-09-14, read-only `gh`): the three watcher-dispatched `agent-maintenance-open-pr` runs of 2026-09-13 (34747321010 codex 0.153.4, 34747320844 claude_code 2.1.236, 34747320689 opencode 1.18.29) all ran on `staging` at `a36a115d`. Their `Acquire complete union / Plan + pin` and `Union → report → validate` check runs are listed on commit `a36a115d`. The packet PRs #206 (head `ab86438c`), #195 (`0f42a57b`), and #205 (`57b7a7f2`) carry only `CI` workflow checks. Those runs predate the T2 gate, but where a dispatched run's checks attach does not depend on the gate, so H3 is settled without a post-T2 dispatch.

items.title: --expect-target-version mismatch fails out-of-packet acquisition runs

prompt: Work item: uaa-0032 — `--expect-target-version` mismatch fails out-of-packet acquisition runs.

Context: T2c (24a95b52) passes `--expect-target-version "$VERSION"` to the gate in `.github/workflows/parity-acquire.yml`. The command exits 2 when the packet request's `detected_release.target_version` differs, and T2c's terminal failure step then fails the job, including `commit: false` dry runs.

Finding (found reading code while writing the 2026-09-13 handoff, H5; confirmed by reading): two documented uses acquire a version that the packet request on `ref` does not name. Plan §13 item 4 proves acquisition on a real runner via `workflow_dispatch` with `ref` defaulting to `staging`. `.github/workflows/parity-promote.yml` tells the maintainer to re-run parity-acquire for a version before promoting it. Both now end red even when acquisition succeeded; artifacts are still uploaded, and committed if `commit: true`.

History: T2b's packet said the gate is informational on a dry run. The T2 adversarial lane's remediation direction allowed either refusing to run or failing; T2c chose fail without weighing these callers. Only the automated lane (open-pr to acquire) is guaranteed to match.

Decided 2026-09-13 by the maintainer: fail only when committing. On a mismatch with `inputs.commit` false, the gate records a non-blocking verdict and emits a `::notice` naming both versions; the job stays green. On a mismatch with `inputs.commit` true, the verdict stays blocking and the job fails after commit and upload, as today.
Steps:

1) Distinguish the version-mismatch exit 2 from other exit 2 failures without parsing message text (for example a dedicated exit code, or a pre-check in the workflow step), so no other validation failure is downgraded on a dry run.
2) Implement the decided routing in the gate step, keeping exit-code capture as `set +e; cmd; s=$?; set -e`.
3) Add or update contract tests binding both branches (commit false: notice, not failed; commit true: failed).
Output: out-of-packet dry runs stay green with a notice; a mismatched committing run still fails.
deliverables: Mismatch routing keyed on inputs.commit
Contract tests for both branches

notes: Found while writing the 2026-09-13 handoff (H5). Confirmed by reading; unreviewed; impact is a maintainer decision.
Maintainer decision 2026-09-13: fail only when committing. Implement in the fix packet that follows the T2c review round.

T2c review round (2026-09-13, both lanes): the mismatch check runs after the request loader's live derivation, so malformed evidence for the request's own version masks the mismatch, and the `..._before_evidence_work` test does not prove its name (a removed report directory makes the loader fall back rather than fail). Mechanism chosen by the lead: compare the request's `detected_release.target_version` before the validated load, and give a mismatch its own exit code (5, `EXIT_TARGET_VERSION_MISMATCH`) so the workflow downgrades only that code on a dry run.

Maintainer decision 2026-09-13: a parity-promote prerequisite re-run (which needs `commit: true` so lockfile pins land) for a version the ref's request does not name is accepted as red-but-committed. Document it where the promote error text points operators.

Implemented in a3c8ce53 (T2d) and hardened in 916c9e9b (T2e): `EXIT_TARGET_VERSION_MISMATCH = 5`, compared before the validated request load (inline tables included); the gate records a non-blocking notice when `COMMIT` is false and a blocking verdict when true. Bound by the behavioural tests in `crates/xtask/tests/c4_spec_audit_gate_behavior.rs` and `crates/xtask/tests/agent_maintenance_audit_status_target_version.rs`. Caveat recorded in the spec: exit 5 says nothing about whether the rest of the request is valid.

items.title: parity-acquire artifact bundle does not match what the run committed

prompt: Work item: uaa-0033 — `parity-acquire` artifact bundle does not match what the run committed.
Context: T2c (24a95b52) made "Upload the committed artifact bundle" in `.github/workflows/parity-acquire.yml` run `always()` so a failing verdict cannot discard the acquisition.

Finding 1 (T2c review, Opus lane, suspected): when an earlier union-job step fails, the upload still succeeds because `wrapper_coverage.json` and `artifacts.lock.json` already exist in the checkout, so `if-no-files-found: error` never trips. The result is an artifact named as the committed bundle that holds nothing this run produced. Preserving completed legs (uaa-0030) makes partial runs more common.
Finding 2 (T2c review, Codex lane): the bundle paths omit `cli_manifests/support_matrix/current.json` and `docs/specs/unified-agent-api/support-matrix.md`, which the commit step stages.
Steps:
1) Decide what the bundle is: exactly the staged commit set, or the run's outputs whether or not they were committed.
2) Name and populate it accordingly, and fail or label it when the run produced nothing new.
3) Bind the bundle path list to the commit step's `git add` list with a contract test.
Output: a bundle whose name and contents agree with what the run actually produced or committed.
deliverables: Defined bundle contents and naming
Contract test binding the bundle to the commit set

notes: Raised in the T2c review round (2026-09-13) by both lanes; accepted and deferred as low severity.

items.title: parity-acquire commit step can push a rebased tree the audit gate never judged

prompt: Work item: uaa-0034 — `parity-acquire` commit step can push a rebased tree the audit gate never judged.

Context: the commit step in `.github/workflows/parity-acquire.yml` retries a rejected push by fetching and rebasing onto `origin/<ref>` up to three times, because the matrix can run for most of an hour while the packet branch moves.

Finding (T2c review, Opus lane, suspected; pre-dates T2c): the maintenance audit gate ran against the checkout before the rebase. If the packet branch gained a change the gate depends on, such as a regenerated maintenance request or coverage evidence, the pushed tree carries a verdict computed against different inputs.
Steps:
1) Determine which packet-branch changes can land during an acquisition run (packet regeneration by `agent-maintenance-open-pr.yml` for the same version is the obvious one).
2) Decide: re-run the gate after a rebase that touched gate inputs, refuse to push when those inputs changed, or document that the verdict is bound to the pre-rebase inputs.
3) Add a contract test for whichever rule is chosen.
Output: a pushed acquisition commit whose gate verdict is known to match its inputs, or a documented binding.
deliverables: Decided rule for gate inputs changed by a rebase
Contract test

notes: Raised in the T2c review round (2026-09-13) by the Opus lane; pre-existing; accepted and deferred as low severity.

items.title: Decide whether opencode's TUI root command is excluded from parity obligations

prompt: Work item: uaa-0035 — Decide whether opencode's TUI root command is excluded from parity obligations.

Context: the 2026-09-14 pre-merge simulation of the audit gate found that opencode 1.18.29's coverage report lists the root command (`path: []`, usage `opencode [project]`, described upstream as "start opencode tui") under `deltas.missing_commands`. opencode's `wrapper_coverage.json` declares only `run`, and `RULES.json` `parity_exclusions` excludes only the root positional arg `project` (category `interactive`). Commit 507cf300 names the row (`commands`, `opencode`, `opencode`) so the audit can evaluate it; the row is now a required uplift (`new_upstream_surface`, writes wrapper/backend/manifest/publication/packet_docs).
Decision (maintainer, ask-first: it changes what closeout obligates): keep the root command as an uplift obligation, or exclude it from parity.

What the contract allows: a newly discovered surface cannot be deferred (`docs/specs/maintenance-request-contract-v1.md` field invariant 3), and `deliberately_unsupported` is an invalid deferral reason, so a debt row is not an option. The non-implementation path is a `RULES.json` parity exclusion: `{"unit": "command", "path": [], "category": "interactive", "note": ...}`. `manifest_report` matches command exclusions exactly (`idx.commands.get(path)` in `crates/xtask/src/manifest_report/report.rs`), so it would exclude only the root command, not `run`, other subcommands, or the 20 root-level flags. No schema change is needed.
Also decide whether the 20 root-level flags (`global_flags`, e.g. `--port`, `--hostname`, `--mdns`) follow the same treatment; excluding the root command does not exclude them.

Triggers — resolve this before the first of: (1) closing any opencode maintenance packet whose audit lists `commands` / `opencode` / `opencode` (T8 or a manual closeout); (2) starting uplift implementation for an opencode packet; (3) editing opencode `RULES.json` `parity_exclusions` or `wrapper_coverage.json` for the root command. Pointers sit at each trigger: spec T5 and T8, and the intro of `docs/specs/unified-agent-api/non-tui-support-debt.md`.

Do not rely on closeout validation to force this decision: by reading, closeout reconciles the frozen audit against live evidence, but it was not verified to require every required uplift to be resolved.
Steps:
1) Get the maintainer decision; record it in this item's notes with the date.

2) If excluded: add the parity exclusion, regenerate the opencode report, and add a test that the root command moves to `excluded_commands` and leaves the audit while `run` and the root flags are unaffected. If kept: leave it on the uplift path.
3) Remove the trigger pointers from spec T5/T8 and the debt inventory intro.
Output: a recorded decision, and an opencode root command that is either excluded with a reason or an owned uplift.
deliverables: Recorded maintainer decision
Exclusion plus regenerated report and test, or confirmation that the root command stays an uplift
Trigger pointers removed once resolved

notes: Raised 2026-09-14 after the pre-merge audit-gate simulation and a ChatGPT Pro consult (advisory). The maintainer approved the root identity and deferred this policy decision, asking that it be tracked at the points where it will be hit.
